source.description: One reviewed eight-panel felt-tip marker contact sheet cropped into seven cumulative process frames and one finished master.
source.notes: Owner-directed correction replacing the non-instructional six-panel v1 sequence. Keep one face-free unbranded alto saxophone on one rising diagonal with one flared bell, bent neck and mouthpiece, exactly seven round key pads, three long key rods, one strap loop, two separate music-note symbols, two sound arcs, three highlights, and one broken shadow. Step 1 must contain only raw construction primitives; no keys, notes, arcs, reflections, embellishments, ink, color, or shadow.

process_strategy: Use eight cumulative stages so the raw bell ellipse and J gesture, rough silhouette, refined instrument structure, pad centers, connecting hardware and sound marks, black ink, marker color, and final reinforcement each receive a distinct visible job. Nothing may disappear after it is introduced, and the final panel may only strengthen established marks and fills.

final_elements.name: raw bell ellipse J gesture tube-width guides neck axis and mouthpiece wedge
final_elements.description: Only pale blue construction primitives: one large tilted bell ellipse, one sweeping J centerline, sparse tube-width cross guides, one raised neck axis, and one small mouthpiece wedge.

final_elements.name: rough flared bell curved tube neck and mouthpiece silhouette
final_elements.description: A loose pale-orange outer contour wrapped around the primitive guides to establish the broad bell, J-curved body tube, raised neck, and mouthpiece.

final_elements.name: refined bell rim bow seam neck collars mouthpiece and key-rail guide
final_elements.description: A doubled bell rim, lower bow seam, two neck-collar bands, clearer mouthpiece planes, and one pale curved guide for the later key rhythm.

final_elements.name: seven round key-pad circles and strap loop
final_elements.description: Exactly seven unfilled round pad circles spaced along the established key-rail guide plus one small strap loop on the outer tube.

final_elements.name: three key rods connector arms key caps two music notes two sound arcs three highlights and broken shadow guide
final_elements.description: Exactly three long rods, short connector arms and small caps attached to the seven pads, two separate music notes, two sound arcs, three reserved highlight shapes, and one pale broken shadow footprint.

final_elements.name: thick black felt-tip keeper lines and restrained bell and hardware hatching
final_elements.description: Handmade black marker traces every established contour and sound mark, with short restrained hatching inside the existing bell and key hardware.

final_elements.name: mustard ochre teal coral and deep-navy marker fills
final_elements.description: Warm mustard and ochre brass, alternating teal and coral pads, coral notes and arcs, and deep-navy mouthpiece and shadow layered around the three reserved paper highlights with visible marker grain.

rejection_checks: Keep one face-free saxophone, one rising diagonal, one crop, and one scale in all eight panels.

Step 1 must show only the bell ellipse, J gesture, tube-width guides, neck axis, and mouthpiece wedge; it must not contain a finished silhouette, keys, rods, notes, arcs, reflections, highlights, shadow, hatching, ink, color, embellishments, text, or decoration.
Each adjacent panel must add a visibly new drawing job at card size; a line-color swap without new structure fails.
Keep one bell, one bent neck, one mouthpiece, seven key pads, three rods, one strap loop, two notes, two sound arcs, three highlights, and one shadow after those elements appear.
No color introduced in an earlier panel may disappear in a later panel, and no black-ink stage may remove previously established keys or sound marks.
Key hardware must stop at the instrument body and body fills must stop at reserved pads and highlights; no taught keeper line may be erased to fake the assembly.
Do not add a face, hands, musician, case, brand mark, words, letters, numbers, extra notes, sticker border, badge frame, label, arrow, signature, or watermark.
The final panel may not introduce a pad, rod, loop, note, arc, highlight, hatch cluster, shadow shape, or color area.
The finish must retain visible felt-tip streaks and imperfect handmade edges rather than vector-clean clip art, polished product rendering, or glossy AI poster art.
